assumptions: The branch lengths are in the units the tree was built in.
limits: Describes the tree as given; a shape statistic on a poorly supported tree describes the estimate, not the clade's history.
The gamma statistic assumes a complete, ultrametric tree.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: The answer is the tree's measurements (tip and node counts, height, the lineage-through-time curve, patristic distances), which the outputs carry; the Stats tab shows them as readouts and writes no reading over them.
bio.jane/contract.question: What shape does this tree have: tips, height, balance, the gamma statistic, lineages through time, and the patristic distances?

description: Describe a tree without rebuilding it: its shape statistics (tips, height, balance, the gamma statistic), the lineages-through-time curve, and the patristic distance matrix — the path lengths through the tree, which is what to compare against the alignment distances that built it.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

newick.description: the tree to describe — wire `newick` from build_tree, or paste one.

name: tree_statistics

ltt.description: lineages-through-time: the points of the curve and the coalescence times behind it

lttPlot.description: the lineages-through-time curve as a plot

patristic.description: labels and the matrix of path lengths between every pair of tips

patristicMap.description: the patristic distances as a heatmap

statistics.description: tips, height, balance and the gamma statistic (with the reason when gamma is undefined for this tree)
